title: Base change morphism for etale extension by zero
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $j:V\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $V'=Y\times_XV$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $j':V'\to Y$ and $f':V'\to V$, so $f\circ j'=j\circ f'$, and $j'$ is etale as a base change of $j$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; let $\square=(f,f',j,j',\mathrm{id})$ be this cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] (top $j'$, bottom $j$). Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules on the small etale site of a scheme $T$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use: the extensions by zero $j_!:\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $j'_!:\Mod(V'_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] with the adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]; the inverse and direct images of sheaves of modules with the adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; the composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]
$$
 L_1=f^{-1}\circ j_!\ \dashv\ R_1=j^{-1}\circ f_*,\qquad L_2=j'_!\circ f'^{-1}\ \dashv\ R_2=f'_*\circ j'^{-1}
$$
(functors $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\rightleftarrows\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$), with units $\eta_1,\eta_2$ and counits $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2$; and the underived exchange transformation $\Ex^0_\square:R_1=j^{-1}f_*\to f'_*j'^{-1}=R_2$ of $\square$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], a natural transformation of functors $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear].

The *base change morphism for extension by zero* of $\square$ is the natural transformation
$$
 \beta=\beta_\square:\ j'_!\circ f'^{-1}=L_2\longrightarrow L_1=f^{-1}\circ j_!
$$
of functors $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ whose conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] with respect to $L_1\dashv R_1$ and $L_2\dashv R_2$ is $\Ex^0_\square$: $\beta^c=\Ex^0_\square$; it exists and is unique because $\tau\mapsto\tau^c$ is a bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Explicitly, for $M\in\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$,
$$
 \beta_M:\ j'_!f'^{-1}M\xrightarrow{L_2(\eta_{1,M})}L_2R_1L_1M\xrightarrow{L_2(\Ex^0_{\square,L_1M})}L_2R_2L_1M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{2,L_1M}}L_1M=f^{-1}j_!M,
$$
i.e. $\beta_M$ is the morphism corresponding under the hom bijection of $L_2\dashv R_2$ to $\Ex^0_{\square,L_1M}\circ\eta_{1,M}:M\to R_1L_1M\to R_2L_1M$, where $\eta_{1,M}=j^{-1}(\eta_{f,j_!M})\circ\eta_{j,M}$. It is natural in $M$. (Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change) identifies $j'_!f'^{-1}$ with $f^{-1}j_!$ by comparing the right adjoints $f'_*(j')^{-1}$ and $j^{-1}f_*$; $\beta$ is the comparison morphism of left adjoints so obtained. It runs from $j'_!f'^{-1}$ to $f^{-1}j_!$, against the direction of an exchange morphism, as the base change map of the source repository does for open immersions.)

proof.text: *The square and the etaleness of $j'$.* Write the fibre product $V'=Y\times_XV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with its projections $j':V'\to Y$, $f':V'\to V$; then $f\circ j'=j\circ f'$. In the notation $(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] (top $X'\xrightarrow{g'}X$, bottom $Y'\xrightarrow{g}Y$, $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$) take $X'=V'$, $X=Y$, $Y=X$, $Y'=V$, $g=j$, $g'=j'$, and the identification $\alpha=\mathrm{id}:V'\to Y\times_XV$; so $\square=(f,f',j,j',\mathrm{id})$ is a cartesian square, with $\theta_\square:f'^{-1}j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^{-1}f^{-1}$. Since $j:V\to X$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $(V,j)$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$, and clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] for $u=f$, $W=V$ says that the base change $Y\times_XV\to Y$, i.e. $j'$, is etale.

source.place: Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), line 11493: the fibre-product square V' = Y x_X V, j', f'

proof.text: *The four adjunctions on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules.* (a) $j$ and $j'$ are etale (step 1), so the extensions by zero $j_!:\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $j'_!:\Mod(V'_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ are defined [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], and by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] they are left adjoint to the inverse images $j^{-1}$, $j'^{-1}$ on sheaves of modules over the constant ring $\Lambda$; write $\eta_j,\varepsilon_j$ and $\eta_{j'},\varepsilon_{j'}$ for units and counits (this is Stacks 03S3(3)). (b) By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3), for $u\in\{f,f'\}$ the module inverse image $u^{-1}$ is left adjoint to the module direct image $u_*$, with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$ those of the adjunction of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. (c) The functor $j^{-1}$ in (a) is the inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] acting on module sheaves: the abelian inverse image of the underlying sheaf, with a $\Lambda_V$-module structure for which $j^{-1}$ of the action map is the action map. By the uniqueness in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](2) this is the module inverse image functor of that proposition, so the right adjoints in (a) and (b), and hence $R_1=j^{-1}f_*$ and $R_2=f'_*j'^{-1}$, are the functors on which [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear] is stated; the same holds for $j'$.

source.place: Definition 03S3 (definition-extension-zero), line 11361, clause (3): j^{-1} on Mod(X_et, Lambda) has the left adjoint j_!; proof of Lemma 03S6, lines 11506-11508

proof.text: *The composite adjunctions.* Apply [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] with $\mathcal A=\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $\mathcal B=\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $\mathcal C=\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $F=j_!\dashv G=j^{-1}$ and $H=f^{-1}\dashv I=f_*$ (step 2): $L_1=f^{-1}\circ j_!\dashv R_1=j^{-1}\circ f_*$, with unit $\eta_{1,M}=j^{-1}(\eta_{f,j_!M})\circ\eta_{j,M}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{1,N}=\varepsilon_{f,N}\circ f^{-1}(\varepsilon_{j,f_*N})$. Apply it again with $\mathcal B=\Mod(V'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $F=f'^{-1}\dashv G=f'_*$ and $H=j'_!\dashv I=j'^{-1}$: $L_2=j'_!\circ f'^{-1}\dashv R_2=f'_*\circ j'^{-1}$, with unit $\eta_{2,M}=f'_*(\eta_{j',f'^{-1}M})\circ\eta_{f',M}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{2,N}=\varepsilon_{j',N}\circ j'_!(\varepsilon_{f',j'^{-1}N})$. Both are adjunctions between $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ (source of $L_i$) and $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ (source of $R_i$), as the statement requires; the formula for $\eta_{1,M}$ in the statement is the one just written.

source.place: proof of Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), lines 11506-11508: j'_! f'^{-1} is left adjoint to f'_*(j')^{-1} and f^{-1} j_! is left adjoint to j^{-1} f_*

proof.text: *$\Ex^0_\square$ is a natural transformation $R_1\to R_2$ of functors on sheaves of modules.* [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] defines $\Ex^0_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*g'^{-1}F$ only for an abelian sheaf $F$ on the top-right scheme of the square (here $Y$), as a morphism of abelian sheaves; with the dictionary of step 1 this is $\Ex^0_{\square,F}:j^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*j'^{-1}F$ on $V_{\Et}$. It does not by itself give a morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_V$-modules, nor naturality. [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear], applied to the cartesian square $\square$ of step 1 (its $X,Y,Y',X',g,g'$ are our $Y,X,V,V',j,j'$), says that for $G\in\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the morphism $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ formed on the underlying abelian sheaf is $\Lambda_V$-linear, $R_1G\to R_2G$, and that these morphisms form a natural transformation $\Ex^0_\square:j^{-1}\circ f_*=R_1\to R_2=f'_*\circ j'^{-1}$ of functors $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$; its functors are those of step 2(c), so $\Ex^0_\square$ is a morphism between the right adjoints of step 3.

source.place: proof of Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), lines 11508-11509: f'_*(j')^{-1} = j^{-1} f_* (the comparison map of the right adjoints, on sheaves of modules)

proof.text: *$\beta$ exists, is unique and natural.* By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], for the two adjunctions $L_1\dashv R_1$, $L_2\dashv R_2$ of step 3, with $\mathcal C=\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal D=\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, the assignment $\tau\mapsto\tau^c$ is a bijection from natural transformations $L_2\to L_1$ to natural transformations $R_1\to R_2$. $\Ex^0_\square$ is one of the latter (step 4), so there is exactly one natural transformation $\beta:L_2=j'_!f'^{-1}\to L_1=f^{-1}j_!$ with $\beta^c=\Ex^0_\square$; being a natural transformation, its components $\beta_M$ are morphisms of $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ natural in $M$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), lines 11506-11509: the comparison of left adjoints obtained from the comparison of right adjoints

proof.text: *The explicit formula.* By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] the conjugate is the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] for $G=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, $H=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$, and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives the inverse of the mate bijection: $\sigma\mapsto(\varepsilon_2HL_1)\circ(L_2\sigma L_1)\circ(L_2G\eta_1)$. With $G,H$ identities and $\sigma=\Ex^0_\square$ this is $\beta_M=\varepsilon_{2,L_1M}\circ L_2(\Ex^0_{\square,L_1M})\circ L_2(\eta_{1,M})$, the composite displayed in the statement, with $\eta_{1,M}=j^{-1}(\eta_{f,j_!M})\circ\eta_{j,M}$ by step 3. The hom bijection of the adjunction $L_2\dashv R_2$ sends $h:M\to R_2N$ to $\varepsilon_{2,N}\circ L_2(h)$ (the counit description of the hom bijection, part of the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], whose hom bijection is the composite of those of $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ and $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$); for $h=\Ex^0_{\square,L_1M}\circ\eta_{1,M}$ and $N=L_1M$, functoriality of $L_2$ gives $\varepsilon_{2,L_1M}\circ L_2(\Ex^0_{\square,L_1M})\circ L_2(\eta_{1,M})=\beta_M$, which is the second description in the statement.

lean.statement: def etaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] {Y V X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (j : V ⟶ X) [Etale j] : upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (pullback.snd f j) ⋙ etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (pullback.fst f j) inferInstance ⟶ etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j inferInstance ⋙ upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f
lean.note: Uses the ModuleCat-valued etale sheaf encoding explicitly allowed by def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves and the stage-2 conventions for six-functor statements; specializes the recorded etaleLowerShriek, upperStar, baseChangeMap and adjunctions to ModuleCat Λ. The chosen fibre product is pullback f j, without extra hypotheses.
